why: Both sides define L(S) the same way: B's LSB is the project's borelNullSigma of its null sets, by rfl. A (universes at 0) states the remark for any σ-ideal 𝒩 (measurableSet_borelNullSigma_iff) and for the project's lebesgueSigma over an abstract SheetNullSets. B states it for its concrete null sets IsNullSB, which are locally n-dimensional Hausdorff-null preimages, as in V9_50. A ⇒ B needs these concrete null sets to form a σ-ideal. They do once locally null subsets of a sheet are closed under countable unions: isSigmaIdeal_of proves the σ-ideal from that and from V9_50's choice independence, re-proved outright here as nullPreimages_of. With this one hypothesis A ⇒ B holds (A_to_B_of_hyp) via A's measurableSet_borelNullSigma_iff. The hypothesis is not proved. In a non-separable E₀ it needs local second countability of the sheets: sc⁺-retract images are locally relatively compact, which the project lacks. It is believed true, so this is missing infrastructure, not a difference of statements. B ⇒ A is vacuous: B does not mention arbitrary σ-ideals or SheetNullSets, so A is re-proved outright (ReProof).
B_issue: B's notion inherits from V9_50 the lack of σ-additivity of IsLocNullB without second countability. B's '⇒' (every member of L(S) is Borel ∆ null) depends on it.
